question.problem: Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation $100{x}^{2}=7.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and collect the like terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}100{x}^{2} & =7 \\ 100{x}^{2}-7 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the difference of squares formula, we factor the left-hand side of our quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}100{x}^{2}-7 & =0 \\ (10x)^{2}-{(\sqrt{7})}^{2} & =0 \\ (10x-\sqrt{7})(10x+\sqrt{7}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the zero product rule, we have

$$
10x-\sqrt{7}=0\,\text{or}\,10x+\sqrt{7}=0.
$$

Then, we solve each equation separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}10x-\sqrt{7} & =0 & \, & \, & 10x+\sqrt{7} & =0 \\ 10x & =\sqrt{7} & \, & \, & 10x & =-\sqrt{7} \\ x & =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{10} & \, & \, & x & =-\frac{\sqrt{7}}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=-\frac{\sqrt{7}}{10},\frac{\sqrt{7}}{10}.$ We can write this even more concisely as $x=\pm \frac{\sqrt{7}}{10}.$
